To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tumour-related changes can be found in the dermis of abdominal skin distant from a distant tumour.

the field effect and extended field effect of a tumour can be demonstrated in human skin, that the field effect of a malignant tumour is due to a change in dermis, and that the extended field effect is due to a tumour-related change in the dermis distant from the tumour.

the field and extended field effect of a tumour can be quantified by histophotometric determination of the ratio between protein reactive sulphur and protein reactive sulphur plus protein reactive thiol in the dermis of abdominal skin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the field effect of skin tumours and the extended field of tumours.
the histophotometric quantitation of the field and extended field effects of human tumours.
tumour-related changes in skin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tumours are associated with a field effect and an extended field effect of changes in the protein thiol status of the skin.
histophotometric investigations on human skin have revealed a field effect of tumour and an extended field effect of a tumour.

the field effect of a tumour is the sum of changes of apparently normal skin in contact with the tumour, and the extended field-effect of a tumour the sum of changes in skin distant from the primary tumour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the field effect and extended field effect of the investigated tumours can be quantified using the DDD-FBB-method.

tumour growth and/or the presence of tumours is associated with a decrease in the total content of PSHr in the skin and with a decrease in PSHr/TRPS in the dermis, which may be due to a decrease in the content of PSHt in the dermis.
tumour-related changes can be found in normal skin, distant from the primary tumour, in patients with tumours, as well as in apparently normal skin from patients without tumours.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tumour-related changes in apparently normal skin distant from the primary tumour are not only restricted to the epithelium but are also found in the dermis.
the field effect of a tumour is a general phenomenon, independent of the state or size of the tumour and of its location, but is limited to a certain distance from the tumour.
histophotometry can be used for the quantitative determination of changes in the field effect of tumors and of the extended field effect.
